locator: pp.3–12 p.12 ('I shall use "physicalism" ... specifically for the doctrine that everything with causal powers is physical, whatever may be true of noncausal realms')
interpretation: Papineau's own working formulation of physicalism, adopted after he limits the causal argument to whatever has physical effects (p.11): everything with causal powers is physical. Read as N3 with P = physical in his indirect sense (DEF-PAPINEAU-PHYSICAL). He leaves open that there are noncausal realms (mathematical objects, value) that are not physical, so he is not committed to N1. He does not say physical things are spatiotemporal: the spatiotemporal N3 is the analyst's instance of the same schema.
attribution: The passage states that everything with causal powers is physical, which is the premise with P = physical.
